name: SpookyHash (centaurean fork of Bob Jenkins' SpookyHash V2)
baseline: xxHash64 (also SipHash, MD5 and Murmur3F rows in the same table)
workload: SMHasher bulk-throughput and small-key speed table (MiB/sec and cycles per hash) in rurban/smhasher, which includes Jenkins' reference SpookyV2_64 code next to xxHash64, SipHash and md5_64.
claimed_speedup: Bulk throughput on the page: SpookyV2_64 13401.13 MiB/sec and Spooky64 13400.95 vs xxHash64 11176.72 (about 1.20x, derived from page data), vs Murmur3F 7104.08 (about 1.9x, derived), vs SipHash 953.51 (about 14x, derived), vs md5_64 360.20 (about 37x, derived). Small keys are not a win: SpookyV2_64 56.18 cycles/hash vs xxHash64 49.67. Project README itself claims only 'long keys hash in 3 bytes per cycle, short keys about 1 byte per cycle, 30 cycle startup', with no baseline.
hardware: README's default sortable table is labelled AMD Ryzen 5 3350G 3.6GHz (the table itself carries no CPU label); compiler and flags not stated in the README
stars_or_usage: 72 stars (archived 2022-12-07); the SMHasher suite holding the numbers has 2.2k stars
tradeoffs: Not cryptographic; 128-bit output with 64- and 32-bit truncations. The fork adds big-endian support and a thread-safe context API, disables unaligned reads by default (changelog 1.0.5), and replaced the memory-copy and rotate code, so its speed may differ from Jenkins' original. Spooky is not a good fit for tiny keys (about 30 cycle startup). Archived, no maintenance.
caveats: The only numbers against real baselines are from rurban/smhasher, which times Jenkins' reference SpookyV1/V2 sources, not this fork; this fork's own test/src/test.c only compares SpookyHash against a trivial addition loop, which is not a recognizable baseline. The algorithm is the same as SpookyV2 (the fork's test vector expected[0] 0x6bf50919 matches V2) but the fork's code was not benchmarked. rurban README flags Spooky (V1) rows with UB and does not state compiler or flags next to the table, hence B not A. SpookyHash loses to xxHash64 on small keys in the same table and to xxh3, wyhash and umash on bulk throughput, so it is not a current speed leader. Fork's test/src/test.c carries a GPL-3.0-or-later header while the library and LICENSE.md are BSD-3-Clause; the fork is a derivative of Bob Jenkins' original (Jenkins' own page could not be opened here, egress blocked), so is_fork_of is left null. Archived 2022-12-07; last commit 2021-03-04 ('Removed org references'), code last changed 2018-01-24.
